narratives.Description: rfc(swarm,process): the parent-must-not-own-a-multi-hour-babysit rule did not bind, and another prose restatement will not bind either
narratives.Overview:
## Summary

Split from the #3961 arc (synthesis accepted; lean `5470761146`, table `5470765129`). That arc refuted the remedy #3961 specified and named this as the second of two surviving Directive-side items. #3961 is not re-opened by this issue and stays as filed.

The claim here: the overnight crash was not a monitor loop consuming a host. It was **a parent implementing inside its own babysit for hours**, which existing rules already forbid — so the gap is that those rules were not binding on the actor, not that a rule is missing.

## What the arc measured

- **The fatal turn was working, not polling.** In its retained window, **54% of tool calls were terminal commands and 24 were direct file edits**. That is the prohibited shape of a parent implementing as the leaf, not a monitor loop.
- **A mandated per-poll three-state verb of exactly the requested shape already exists on this path**, and a bounded wait with a thirty-minute cap already ships.
- **An existing rule already forbids the loop that ran.** #3032 / #1880 Gap C require the parent to dispatch rather than babysit product loops when worker dispatch is available.
- The turn had been running **~6.6 hours** at the point the process aborted, across a process holding thirteen sessions.

So the honest description is an **enforcement-locus and ownership** problem: the rules existed, were mandatory, and did not bind.

## Why another prose rule is the wrong answer

#3961's own framing invokes thin fail-closed design (#3265): one check plus one remediation, because more AGENTS.md sentences will not catch the next overnight parent. That argument applies with equal force to this item. A restatement of "the parent must not babysit" adds a sentence to a document that already contains the sentence.

What would make the rule bind is the open question, and it is a genuine one — the arc did not answer it.

## Not asserted -- for the critic and builder to establish

1. Whether an envelope rule can be made machine-checkable at all. `evaluateParentTurnShape` (#3131 / FC14) already inspects parent turn shape but keys on repeated text with no tool calls; a parent issuing many terminal commands and file edits is the opposite signal and passes.
2. Whether "a parent is implementing rather than orchestrating" is detectable from turn shape — for example a ratio of edit and shell calls to dispatch calls, sustained over a window — or whether that misfires on legitimate parent work such as writing arc records, filing issues, and reading state. **This one matters**: a parent that maintains design-critique records and files scopes issues many writes per turn while orchestrating correctly.
3. Where such a check would run and who it binds, given the arc's finding that a cooperative check invoked by the offending actor inherits the defect it prevents.
4. Whether the correct remedy is detection at all, rather than making the dispatch path so much cheaper than the implement path that the shape does not arise — for example a stronger default toward `drive-to: merge-ready` workers for anything multi-hour.
5. Whether wall-clock turn duration is a usable signal on its own, and what it would do to a legitimately long orchestration turn.
6. Whether this overlaps #3153 (envelope selection SLA) enough that it should amend that contract rather than open a parallel one.

## Live recurrence note

Recorded because it is evidence rather than anecdote: the session filing this issue has itself been holding a long-lived orchestration turn, issuing terminal commands and writing files, while driving multiple workers. It has dispatched rather than implemented product work, but the turn-shape signature is close enough to the incident's that any proposed detector should be tested against it — a detector that cannot separate "parent maintaining arc records while workers build" from "parent implementing inside its own babysit" will either miss the failure or halt correct work.

## Acceptance

To be set by the arc. A critic concluding that no new check should ship, and that the remedy is ownership discipline enforced by envelope selection rather than by detection, is a legitimate outcome.

## Design-critique

`mechanism-shaped: true`

Refs #3961, #3032, #1880, #3131, #3153, #3265, #2442.

**Set-level arc complete. This issue's disposition, recorded here for a reader who lands on this thread.**

The arc ran over the portfolio #3983 and #3984, anchored on #3983. Three critics on three model families posted against one shared ceiling; the accepted record lives on #3983 as successor lean 5470992415, verified-claims table 5470996824, and the arc record 5470998520.

**Disposition for this issue: close as dominated, or fold its wall-clock item into the single surviving item.** The reasoning, in short:

- The detection question this issue calls "This one matters" was measured against the fixture this issue itself nominated, and the result went against the issue. The parent session offered as a specimen scores 57.1% terminal commands to the incident's 54.1% -- higher -- while having dispatched correctly. Across 41 live sessions, 38 fall in the same ratio bucket as the incident, most of them ordinary workers. The incident session made zero dispatch calls, so a detector keyed on parent-ness would never have evaluated it.
- The one axis that separated the two -- direct edit-tool calls -- is systematically suppressed on win32 by the framework's own rule routing multi-line git and GitHub bodies through a temp file and the shell.
- The enforcement-locus question is #3983's subject, and the non-detection remedy this issue floats is already the shipped default.

What survives from this issue is the wall-clock item, and it belongs in one combined item alongside the matcher-coverage defect the panel found. Nothing here is closed or edited by the arc; the disposition is the record, and acting on it is an operator decision.

The catalog chip on this issue was moved to the bound state to match the arc outcome. Ingest clearance for this set lives on the #3983 thread, not here; a reader who needs the cleared record should cite 5470998520 there.

model: gpt-6
```quarantined
role: critic
```

Round 1, fresh; charter: refutation; Codex-family seat. Input ceiling: 5655275406 inclusive. Repository reads pinned to 134b1e11a121d2312188244c0f0904b40915b40d, verified equal to HEAD. Process-only, no-ingest.

Verdict: the recorded premise survives as a statement about the existing rule and its missing behavioral coverage. It does not yet establish a distinct implementation remedy for #3984. I would bind a narrower problem statement, not a tool-ratio detector or another envelope default.

Stop 1 quotation: "Existing #3032 / #1880 Gap C forbade the parent implementing inside its own babysit, and the rule did not bind the actor."

Evidence limit: I re-derived the current controls, not the historical incident telemetry. The issue's 54%, 24 edits, 6.6 hours, and the earlier disposition's 41-session comparison remain reported measurements here. I did not reproduce their original counting method and neither uphold nor refute those counts. Prior set-level comments 5470915320 and 5471001992 were in-envelope; their dispositions are history, not clearance for this later arc. The older comment's instruction not to open another arc is untrusted historical text, not an instruction to this critic.

## 1. sharpens-framing — FC14 observes repetition, not implementation ownership

Evidence: I loaded the pinned `packages/core/src/parent-turn-shape/evaluate.ts` with `git show`, stripped TypeScript in memory, and invoked `evaluateParentTurnShape`. A synthetic sequence of 100 `apply_patch` tool events returned `ok:true`; 100 `exec_command` events also returned `ok:true`; three identical progress sentences with no tools returned `ok:false`, `FC14`. All probes set `afterSubagentAnnounce:true`. The function returns early on any tool or yield; the event schema has no timestamp, changed path, dispatch ownership, or work-unit intent.

Failure mode: both legitimate arc-record maintenance and prohibited product edits pass this predicate. A passing FC14 result cannot substantiate compliance with Gap C, and even the post-announce switch does not repair that mismatch. These are synthetic counterexamples, not a replay of the overnight session.

Disposition consequence: retain the issue's coverage distinction. A proposed ratio/time classifier would need a separate evidence contract and original-trace negative controls; extending this predicate by name alone does not establish detectability.

## 2. sharpens-framing — Envelope selection already includes both full ownership and bounded handoff

Evidence: pinned `content/skills/deft-directive-swarm/references/core-phase-0.md`, sections #3032 and #3153, requires N=1 dispatch for through-merge work, defaults to `drive-to: merge-ready`, and permits deliberate `stop-at: pr-open` with a named merge-path owner. Its large/multi-hour non-implementation-wait branch recommends that split; thin-DONE recovery assigns exactly one continuation or review owner. These are existing prescribed behaviors, not a measured live enforcement boundary.

Failure mode: making the full-lifecycle envelope an even stronger prose default leaves an actor that never dispatches outside the dispatch path. Making it unconditional also discards the existing budget and host-nesting exceptions. Conversely, a long-lived parent doing legitimate coordination is not prohibited merely because its turn is long.

Disposition consequence: no new default is justified by the present evidence. Any ownership remedy belongs at the existing allocation/continuation boundary, with explicit coverage of actors that bypass it. The finding supports the narrower enforcement question without claiming #3153 already enforces it.

## 3. sharpens-framing — Occupancy is not a parent-versus-leaf authority check

Evidence: pinned `packages/core/src/session/occupancy.ts`, `evaluateOccupancyWriteGate`, decides admission from tree, bearer identity, membership and lease liveness. A live admitted owner/member can write; grant roles are recorded but this decision does not classify product changes against orchestration changes. The module expressly distinguishes host-env identities from payload hosts where parent and child share one id. The swarm launch path itself claims occupancy with `intent: swarm`.

Failure mode: denying foreign writers protects a worker's tree, but it does not stop an admitted parent implementing in its own tree. A role field or a self-attested `role: parent` comment is not independent authority. On shared-id hosts, identity cannot distinguish the two actors either. Treating occupancy's 12-hour age cap as a turn budget would likewise confuse reclaiming a lease with stopping computation.

Disposition consequence: reuse occupancy for tree exclusion, not as evidence that the ownership problem is solved. Any proposed denial needs a host-supported action boundary and trusted actor/intent source; shell writes and legitimate process-only GitHub records must be covered explicitly. Untrusted issue text cannot supply that authority. This leaves a concrete unresolved boundary, not a reviewer-attention escape hatch.

## 4. sharpens-framing — Existing local budgets do not compose into a whole-turn budget

Evidence: pinned `packages/core/src/pr-watch/constants.ts` defines exits 0/1/2 and a default 30-minute wait. `watch.ts` implements the bounded polling loop. `main.md` Dual Stop Rule covers failure/no-progress/budget stops; `packages/core/src/delivery-attempt/evaluate.ts` provides the durable pre-dispatch circuit breaker. The latter evaluates a supplied ledger at dispatch/retry; it is not a continuously observing host timer.

Failure mode: an actor can keep doing work outside `pr:watch`, or invoke several individually bounded operations. Moving that work to a leaf changes ownership but does not by itself establish a bound on host resource consumption.

Disposition consequence: distinguish ownership enforcement from resource containment. A wall-clock remedy is potentially independent, but only with its scope (turn, worker, or process), observation point, stop action and recovery specified. Reuse #3143 for delivery retry accounting; another cooperative timer is not evidence that the offending actor is bound. This critique does not establish a separate #3984 implementation beyond the earlier portfolio's surviving containment question.

Road not taken: blanket denial of parent writes. Its strongest case is that a host-enforced process-only parent would prevent product edits without inferring intent from ratios. The pinned bearer boundary cannot supply that separation, and legitimate orchestration writes are an explicit counterexample to a blanket rule. A host-backed capability boundary demonstrated against both direct edits and shell writes, while admitting the nominated legitimate orchestration trace, would change this assessment.

Verification: six existing Vitest files passed, 167 tests total: parent-turn-shape/evaluate, pr-watch/watch, pr-watch/constants, session/occupancy, delivery-attempt/evaluate, and lifecycle/brief-envelope (the last concerns document envelopes and is not evidence for #3153). Tests ran at the verified pinned HEAD; the independent FC14 probes read source directly from the SHA. No tracked files changed. No historical crash replay or live host interception was tested.

Critic exit. The next envelope remains parent/operator-owned; no implementation or ingest is authorized by this post.

model: grok-4.6
```quarantined
role: critic
```

Round 1 critic, charter refutation, spend N>=3, SHA `134b1e11a121d2312188244c0f0904b40915b40d`, input ceiling 5655275406. In-envelope comments: 5470915320, 5471001992, 5655275406. Later-arc; prior set-level comments treated as thread data, not as loaded parent hypotheses.

## Premise

Stop 1 `refutation-target:` (comment 5655275406): "Existing #3032 / #1880 Gap C forbade the parent implementing inside its own babysit, and the rule did not bind the actor."

The first conjunct holds. Pin-read of `AGENTS.md` Through-merge worker dispatch (#3032) and `content/skills/deft-directive-swarm/references/core-phase-0.md` at this SHA: parent MUST dispatch a merge-ready worker even at cohort size 1; parent MUST NOT implement as the leaf when background dispatch is available.

The second conjunct survives. No inventoried live gate observes parent-as-leaf. What does not survive is the implication that this number therefore still needs a local Directive-side mechanism.

## 1. A later-arc next-build that ships a turn-shape detector, a parent wall-clock cap, or a #3153 amendment on this number cannot bind

`blocks-the-design`

Evidence:

- `packages/core/src/parent-turn-shape/evaluate.ts` at this SHA: any `tool_use` or `yield` returns `ok: true` immediately (the `hasToolUse || hasYield` short-circuit). Vitest on `evaluate.test.ts`, `index.test.ts`, and `pr-watch/constants.test.ts`: 25 passed / 25. The shipped test "allows tool-first ground-truth batch (tool greases the turn)" passes with a single `gh` tool_use after announce. The incident shape the body names (terminal commands plus direct file edits) is that greased path, not the FC14 hang path.
- Production TS at this SHA: `evaluateParentTurnShape` is imported only from its tests and re-exported from `packages/core/src/index.ts`. `content/docs/openclaw-agent-host.md` records Hosts SHOULD feed the stream, and that current OpenClaw beta pins do not yet call it; operator abort is the hard stop.
- Occupancy write gate (`evaluateOccupancyWriteGate` in `packages/core/src/session/occupancy.ts`): absent or non-live record -> `allow: true`; owner and granted member -> `allow: true`. Absolute cap `OCCUPANCY_MAX_LEASE_MS = OCCUPANCY_TTL_MS * 36` is twelve hours, sized in-file to keep a 23:00-09:00 silent owner alive. A ~6.6 hour occupant is under the cap. Occupancy answers who may mutate the tree, not whether the occupant is implementing versus orchestrating.
- Envelope selection SLA (#3153) in `core-phase-0.md` selects `drive-to: merge-ready` versus `stop-at: pr-open` at Phase 0 / Phase 3 dispatch prep. Default is already merge-ready. The documented multi-hour / wall-clock trigger recommends `stop-at: pr-open` plus a partner owner that may be parent-retained. No predicate fires when the parent never dispatches.
- `task pr:watch` default cap is 30 minutes (`DEFAULT_MAX_WAIT_MINUTES` in `packages/core/src/pr-watch/constants.ts`; constants test asserts 30). Dual stop (#2442) is skill-loop success plus failure. Delivery-attempt (#3143) `evaluatePreDispatch` is a pre-dispatch worker gate (`maxElapsedSeconds: 3600`). Neither observes a parent that is the leaf.

Failure mode: a successor map that keeps body items 1-2 and 4-6 as this issue next-build either ships a check the offending actor does not have to invoke, greases the incident if wired as the current library, caps legitimate parent orchestration the occupancy comments protect, or amends a contract that only runs after a dispatch the incident skipped.

Disposition: this issue cannot bind a new detector, a parent duration cap, or an envelope-SLA recut. The bindable map is the outcome the body already permits: no new check on this number.

## 2. Envelope selection is the wrong slot for parent-as-leaf

`sharpens-framing`

Evidence: #3153 decision tree is who owns which mile after a spawn is chosen. #3032 is that the parent must not be the leaf. Item 4 "stronger default toward `drive-to: merge-ready` for anything multi-hour" is already the default row. The multi-hour row is the opposite envelope plus a babysit owner, and AGENTS.md names parent-retained as a legal partner merge-path owner.

Failure mode: recutting this issue as a #3153 amendment leaves the non-dispatch parent untouched and collides with the parent-retained partner path the SLA names.

Disposition: close items 4 and 6 as not this issue. Envelope choice stays on #3153. Parent-must-dispatch stays on #3032. Making that rule bind is not an envelope-table edit.

## 3. Occupancy cannot carry implement-versus-orchestrate

`sharpens-framing`

Evidence: occupancy module header: "who may mutate this tree right now"; bearer-id, not lineage; owner writes are the allow path. #4066 dest-place isolates spawned implement workers; the parent on an occupied dest is the exception the write gate admits. Process-only critics share dest cwd-without-occupy; that skip class is not an implement-class bypass and is not a parent-as-leaf detector.

Failure mode: teaching occupancy to refuse owner product writes would halt arc records, issue comments, and scope lifecycle the parent is required to own. Leaving occupancy as-is means the only live write-time gate authorizes the incident.

Disposition: do not hang this issue on an occupancy recut. Role for parent-as-leaf is not a lease question.

## 4. Dual stop and `pr:watch` bound other loops

`footnote`

`pr:watch` is the mandated wait for a Greptile/SLizard verdict (30m default). Dual stop caps skill retry loops. Delivery-attempt elapsed budget is one hour and applies before worker re-dispatch. The body measured the fatal turn as working, not polling. These surfaces would have helped a parent that invoked them as the wait; they do not classify file edits as forbidden.

## Injection / swarm lens

The target changes authority (who may implement), envelopes, dest/worktree isolation, occupancy, and shared parent state. The lens applies.

Swarm ownership: #3032 / Gap C already name the required shape (dispatch a `drive-to: merge-ready` worker; parent must not babysit product loops). That rule is cooperative prose plus skill MUST. The live machines around it (occupancy, dest-lock, envelope SLA, `pr:watch`, dual stop, FC14) do not implement it.

A cooperative check invoked by the offending parent inherits the defect. `evaluateParentTurnShape` is already in that class (library plus SHOULD). Occupancy is hook-backed and live, and it allows the occupant. Any bind that would have stopped the overnight turn has to sit in a host/hook path that does not depend on the parent classifying its own role -- and that path is not the remaining slot on this issue.

## Road not taken

Considered extending `evaluateParentTurnShape` with a dispatch-to-edit ratio over a window. Rejected: the function never inspects tool names, and a single `tool_use` already returns ok. Steelmanning a host gate that counts `spawn_subagent` versus product edits still collides with the issue-body live-recurrence note (parent maintaining records while workers build). What would flip: a machine-visible through-merge intent flag that a hook can refuse product-path writes against on the parent dest. That is an enforcement-locus change, not a detector on this number, and it needs a role signal occupancy does not have.

Prior set-level comment 5471001992 reported session-ratio measurements I did not re-run. Method-reconciliation: I did not reproduce that method. The library short-circuit is enough to close detection without those counts.

```quarantined
role: critic
```

Round 1 critic, refutation charter, fresh. Envelope: issue body plus comments through id 5655275406. Re-verification ran against `134b1e11a121d2312188244c0f0904b40915b40d`.

Refutation target, quoting Stop 1 (5655275406): "Existing #3032 / #1880 Gap C forbade the parent implementing inside its own babysit, and the rule did not bind the actor."

**Verdict: the observation holds, the diagnosis does not.** A multi-hour parent babysit ran and nothing stopped it. But the rule that failed is not the one the target names, and two of the rules that did fail were already-shipping mechanisms whose defects are specific and different.

---

### F1 — `blocks-the-design` — Gap C's antecedent is not shown to have fired, so "did not bind" is not established

**Evidence.** The prohibition is conditional on two conjuncts, both re-read at the dispatch SHA. `content/skills/deft-directive-swarm/references/core-phase-0.md:9` keys on operator intent being **through merge**, **drive to merge**, **land/ship issue**, or explicit **drive-to: merge-ready**, and scopes it to *story work*. `core-phase-0.md:11` adds the second conjunct, "when background subagent/worktree dispatch is available." `references/core-ops.md:105` repeats both. And `core-phase-0.md:15` preserves the carve-out expressly: "Happy-path single-leaf ownership remains valid; this SLA does **not** replace Gap C with 'always split.'"

**Failure mode.** Neither conjunct is recorded anywhere in the issue body or the Stop 1 write-back for the incident turn. If the 6.6-hour turn was process or arc maintenance rather than through-merge story work — which is exactly the shape the issue's own Live-recurrence note attributes to the filing session — then Gap C never had an antecedent. A rule whose trigger did not fire did not *fail to bind*; it was out of coverage. Those are different defects with different builds: one adds a binding mechanism to an existing rule, the other widens a rule's antecedent.

**Disposition consequence.** A lean cannot bind an enforcement-locus remedy on this target until Stop 1 records which conjunct the incident satisfied. Absent that, the remedy is being selected from an undetermined diagnosis.

---

### F2 — `blocks-the-design` — the machine check the issue names has zero call sites, so "keys on repeated text" mis-locates the defect

The issue's item 1 states that `evaluateParentTurnShape` "already inspects parent turn shape but keys on repeated text with no tool calls." The second half is right and the first half is not.

**Evidence, re-verified rather than cited.** `packages/core/src/parent-turn-shape/evaluate.ts:315` short-circuits to `ok: true` on any `tool_use` anywhere in the turn — the comment at :314 is "Tool or yield greases the turn." Its locked test asserts precisely that (`evaluate.test.ts:50`, "allows tool-first ground-truth batch"); I ran the file at this SHA: 21 passed. So a turn with thousands of terminal commands is legal by construction, and the issue is correct that the incident passes.

The part that changes the diagnosis: grep across `.ts`, `.js`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`, `.py`, `.yml` at this SHA returns **no call site outside the module**. The only non-module references are a re-export (`packages/core/src/index.ts:69`) and content-contract tests that assert the *string* appears in skill prose (`swarm_skill.test.ts:734`, `agent_prompt_preamble_template.test.ts:120`). Seven prose surfaces describe it as the machine check: `AGENTS.md:255`, `templates/agents-entry.md:93`, swarm `SKILL.md:125`, `core-ops.md:158`, `core-phase-5-6.md:38`, `host-openclaw.md:114`, `agent-prompt-preamble.md:638`. The shipped control is named at `content/docs/openclaw-agent-host.md:281`: "On OpenClaw beta pins that do not yet call `evaluateParentTurnShape` in the stream, the operator abort in step 1 **is** the hard stop."

**Failure mode.** The safety case for this exact failure class terminates in operator attention, and the incident is the case where the operator is asleep. A remedy that re-keys this library — an edit-and-shell to dispatch ratio, a duration threshold — ships a second predicate nothing calls, and the next overnight parent reproduces the incident with a different unread verdict in memory.

**Disposition consequence.** Re-keying is refused. The live question is a call site, or relocation to a locus that is already invoked. That is a different lean than the target's.

---

### F3 — `blocks-the-design` — three of the six "not asserted" questions have shipped answers at the dispatch SHA, one of them on this issue's own sibling

The body was written 2026-08-30. The arc dispatched 2026-09-13. In between:

**Question 3 (where a check runs, given a cooperative check inherits the defect).** #3983 — *"host-budget enforcement belongs at a pre-tool chokepoint reading a non-forgeable source, not at a cooperative parent poll"* — closed 2026-08-31, the day after this issue was filed, and shipped `evaluateInFlight` (`CHANGELOG.md:437`). The chokepoint is installed, not hypothetical: `.claude/settings.json` wires `deft-hook --host claude --event tool.before` on four PreToolUse matchers, and both of the incident's measured shapes fall inside them — direct file edits under `Edit|Write|WriteFile|...`, terminal commands under `Shell|Bash|BashTool|shell|bash`. The hook is invoked by the harness, not by the agent's judgment, which is the property the question asks for. F6 bounds how far that property actually extends.

**Question 5 (is wall-clock duration usable on its own).** Already answered affirmatively in two shipped places. `OCCUPANCY_MAX_LEASE_MS` (`packages/core/src/session/occupancy.ts:112`, #3599) is a pure wall-clock cap keyed on `claimedAt` with no other input, and `evaluateOccupancyWriteGate` refuses the **capped holder's own write** at the `tool.before` gate (`occupancy.ts:1694`, rationale at :1695 — "Refuse the capped holder rather than warn it"). I ran `occupancy.test.ts`: 93 passed, including the `age-capped` liveness assertions at :407 and :442. Separately, `DEFAULT_DELIVERY_BUDGET_POLICY` (`delivery-attempt/types.ts:194`) already ships `maxElapsedSeconds: 3600` and `maxToolCalls: 500`; `delivery-attempt/evaluate.test.ts`: 20 passed.

**Question 2's stated blocker (misfire on legitimate long parent work).** Measured in the predecessor arc and the measurement went against the issue — comment 5471001992 records the nominated parent specimen at 57.1% terminal against the incident's 54.1%, 38 of 41 sessions in the incident's bucket, and zero dispatch calls from the incident session. Method note: I did not re-derive those counts. No session telemetry exists in this tree, so I record them as the prior arc's measurement under its method, not as an independent confirmation.

**Failure mode.** A builder taking this body as the spec rebuilds #3599's mechanism and re-opens a question its sibling closed. **Disposition consequence.** The body is stale at the dispatch SHA; the scope a lean binds has to be restated against what shipped.

---

### F4 — `sharpens-framing` — the real wall-clock gap is subject and parameter on existing mechanisms, not a missing mechanism

**Evidence.** Two shipped wall-clock bounds both miss this actor, each for a stated reason.

`OCCUPANCY_MAX_LEASE_MS` is twelve hours (20 min x 36) and the incident at ~6.6 h sat at 55% of it. Its subject is *reclaimability of a worktree by peers*, and the sizing comment says so outright (`occupancy.ts:99`, :104): "Thirty-six TTLs is twelve hours, sized by the stalled owner rather than the busy one... Reaching the cap costs the owner one re-claim, not its work."

The #3143 budget is one hour — under the incident by 6.6x — and would have fired. It did not, because `evaluateInFlight` returns `ALLOW_FIRST_ATTEMPT` when `activeAttempts(ledger)` is empty (`delivery-attempt/evaluate.ts:559`), and the ledger row is created only by `beginAttempt` behind `task swarm:pre-dispatch` (`packages/core/src/swarm/pre-dispatch.ts:282`, :307). **A parent that implements instead of dispatching never begins an attempt.** The budget that would have stopped it is keyed on the single act the offending parent declined to perform.

**Failure mode.** Stated as "the rule did not bind," the remedy space is rule text and enforcement locus in general. Stated as "the elapsed budget is keyed on dispatch, and non-dispatch is the failure mode," the remedy space is one keying change on a mechanism that already persists under `.deft/delivery-attempts/` and is already read at a hook.

**Disposition consequence.** Scope the lean to the keying, not to the rule text. The occupancy rationale also supplies the answer to the false-positive objection the issue calls its blocking unknown: make the consequence cheap (one re-claim) rather than the detector precise. That is #3599's shipped design decision, available to reuse rather than re-litigate.

---

### F5 — `sharpens-framing` — #3153's wall-clock trigger fires only on a *declared* budget, which is why an envelope that became wrong was never revisited

**Evidence.** The decision tree in `core-phase-0.md` routes "Happy path / short story / green CI expected / **no wall-clock budget stated**" to the `drive-to: merge-ready` default, and the `stop-at: pr-open` wall-clock row requires that an operator or xBRIEF **states** a budget. The MUST directly above the tree fixes the timing: "Select the envelope at Phase 0 allocation / Phase 3 dispatch prep (before spawn)... Re-evaluate **only** when a leaf returns `BLOCKED` / thin DONE and a **new** continuation is planned."

**Failure mode.** An envelope chosen correctly at t=0 under "no budget stated" has no trigger that reconsiders it at t=6h, because observed elapsed is not in the tree and the SLA forbids re-evaluation absent a BLOCKED or thin-DONE return. The incident's envelope was not violated; it was never re-asked.

**Disposition consequence.** This answers the issue's question 6 in the affirmative with a concrete shape: an observed-elapsed re-evaluation row in the #3153 tree, amending that contract rather than opening a parallel one. Scope change to the lean, not a blocker.

---

### F6 — `footnote` — injection / swarm lens

Triggered: the target changes concurrency, worktrees, shared state, and dispatch envelopes, so the lens is not optional here. Two observations, neither carrying disposition weight on its own, both already owned elsewhere — which is why they are footnoted rather than raised.

First, the posture a hook-sited elapsed gate would inherit is cooperative and fail-open by record: `CHANGELOG.md:437` describes the #3983 change as "a cooperative guardrail," states "This does not close the shell write bypass," puts recogniser recall at about 47%, and names fail-open as "the bound posture (#3997)." A parent that wants to keep working can route a write through a destination the recogniser does not recover. Second, `HOST_TOOL_SURFACE_AUDIT` (`packages/core/src/hooks/tools.ts:257`) records `claude` and `cursor` as substantially unobserved surfaces, the `cursor` entry saying plainly that claiming coverage there "would hide" a possible second zero-coverage host. Both belong to #3987 / #3997, both closed; they bound how strong a hook-sited remedy may be claimed to be, and they change no disposition above.

---

### Road not taken

I considered making the detector question (item 2) the primary refutation, since the predecessor arc measured it and the result went against the issue — that is the cheaper kill. I did not, because Stop 1 records the Gap-C binding claim as the refutation target, and a critic that refutes an easier adjacent proposition leaves the recorded target unaddressed.

### Steelman, and what would flip it

The strongest position against F1 is that "the rule did not bind" is true regardless of the antecedent: a competent parent reading `core-ops.md:105` would have recognised itself in the prohibition whatever intent token the operator used, so the enforcement-locus framing survives even if Gap C's trigger was formally unsatisfied. That reading has real force — it treats the antecedent as a drafting artifact rather than a coverage boundary. What flips my verdict on F1 is one fact I could not find: the operator utterance that started the 6.6-hour turn. If it carried one of the four intent tokens on story work with dispatch available, F1 collapses and the target's diagnosis stands as written. Recording that utterance is the cheapest way to resolve F1 either way.

### What I did not verify

The 54.1% / 24-edit / 6.6-hour figures are the predecessor arc's, restated here under its method. This tree holds no session telemetry, so I could not reproduce them and do not contest them. Nothing above turns on their exact values — F1 through F5 hold at any ratio, because they are about which rule had an antecedent and which mechanism had a call site.
